statement: Show that $x^3+x-1=0$ has a root in $(0,1)$ and use one iteration of the Newton-Raphson method, starting from $x_0=1$, to estimate it.
solution:
Let $f(x)=x^3+x-1$. Then $f(0)=-1<0$ and $f(1)=1>0$, so by the intermediate value theorem there is a root in $(0,1)$.

$f'(x)=3x^2+1$. The Newton-Raphson iteration is $x_{n+1}=x_n-\dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$. From $x_0=1$:
$$x_1=1-\frac{f(1)}{f'(1)}=1-\frac{1+1-1}{3+1}=1-\frac14=\frac34=0.75.$$
So the estimate after one iteration is $0.75$.
hints: Check f(0) and f(1) have opposite signs.
